chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim; he is his eye, his mirror, and his guide. He does not betray him, nor deceive him, nor oppress him, nor lie to him, nor backbite him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five key ethical responsibilities a Muslim has towards his brother in faith according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the concept of brotherhood by defining the Muslim as the 'eye, mirror, and guide' of his brother, emphasizing mutual spiritual oversight and integrity. The five prohibitions—betrayal, deception, oppression, lying, and backbiting—serve as practical safeguards for maintaining the purity of the communal bond, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (ethics) as the foundation of faith. This narration underscores that true brotherhood requires not just nominal affiliation but active protection of one another's honor and truth.
